one_liner: What one full shutter press does: one frame, a burst, or a timer.

options.meaning: Z5II about 14 fps (15 silent); Z50II about 11 fps (15 silent). Exposure may vary within the burst.

one_liner: Saves frames from before you fully pressed the shutter (HSFC+ modes).
what_it_does: In high-speed frame capture+, the camera buffers frames while the shutter is half-pressed; on full press it saves the last N seconds (pre-release burst) plus a set time after (post-release burst). Buffering times out after about 90 s of continuous half-press (Z50II manual).

options.value: Pre-release burst: None or a time
options.meaning: How many seconds before full press are kept.
options.use_when: 0.3-0.5 s for bird take-offs; longer = more culling.

options.value: Post-release burst: 1 s / 2 s / 3 s / Max.
options.meaning: How long shooting continues after full press.
options.use_when: 1-2 s keeps file counts sane; Max for long actions.

when_to_change: Set before a perched-bird wait; check the L icon shows a green dot while half-pressed.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light

suggested.value: Pre 0.3 s, post 1 s for a jump

body_differences: Present as d3 on all three; applies only in HSFC+ modes. Z8 FW 2.00 lengthened pre-release buffering.
gotchas: After ~90 s of half-press it cancels; lift and half-press again (Z50II manual).
If you full-press sooner than the pre-release time, only the buffered portion is saved.
research_notes: Exact pre-release time values per body not retrieved.

name: d6 Shutter type (mechanical / EFCS / auto)

menu_path.z5ii: Custom Settings menu > d Shooting/display > d6 Shutter type
menu_path.z50ii: Custom Settings menu > d Shooting/display > d6 Shutter type

one_liner: Pick mechanical, electronic front-curtain, or let the camera choose.
what_it_does: Mechanical uses both physical curtains: no rolling-shutter distortion and no LED banding from the sensor readout. Electronic front-curtain (EFCS) starts the exposure electronically to avoid shutter shock at slow speeds but limits the top speed to 1/2000 s. Auto picks EFCS at slow speeds. The fully electronic shutter is reached via Silent mode, not here.

options.meaning: Camera uses EFCS at slow speeds, mechanical at fast.
options.use_when: Default for general shooting.
LED-lit stage, flash, fast panning - no rolling distortion.
Tripod moon/landscape/macro at 1/15-1/250 where shutter shock blurs.

when_to_change: Mechanical under LED stage lighting or with flash; EFCS on a tripod with long lenses or macro.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light
suggested.value: Mechanical (Z5II) - avoids e-shutter banding; Z8 n/a

body_differences: Z8 has no mechanical shutter and no d6 Shutter type for stills (only an electronic shutter with a sensor shield). Z5II and Z50II have Auto / Mechanical / EFCS; their full electronic shutter is used in Silent mode.
gotchas: EFCS caps shutter speed at 1/2000 s (Z50II manual).
Mechanical shutter may be unavailable with some lenses (Z50II manual).
High-frequency flicker reduction range depends on this setting.
research_notes: Z5II d6 option labels assumed to match the Z50II (both menu indexes list d6 Shutter type; Z5II spec lists mechanical, EFCS and electronic shutter types).

name: Silent mode (electronic shutter)

menu_path.z8: Setup menu > Silent mode (not confirmed in the current manual index - verify)

one_liner: Uses the electronic shutter and mutes camera sounds for quiet shooting.
what_it_does: On the Z5II/Z50II, Silent mode switches to the fully electronic shutter regardless of d6 and mutes beeps. That removes shutter noise and vibration but brings rolling-shutter distortion, banding under flickering/LED light, no flash and no photo flicker reduction. On the Z8 the shutter is always electronic, so its silence comes from turning off the simulated shutter sound.

options.use_when: Quiet ceremonies, sleeping baby, timid wildlife.
LED stage light, flash, fast pans.

when_to_change: Turn ON for silence when light is natural/continuous; OFF under LED/fluorescent light or for fast motion on the Z5II/Z50II.

suggested.value: Z5II OFF (banding risk), accept mechanical shutter noise; Z8 silent is fine but check banding
ON (no shutter shock); Z5II EFCS also fine

gotchas: Z50II: flash won't fire; Long exposure NR and Photo flicker reduction disabled; banding under fluorescent/mercury/sodium light; motion distortion.
Aperture and AF motors are still audible.
Focus shift and interval timer have their own e-shutter options that still make a sound unless volume is 0.

name: Photo flicker reduction

menu_path.z8: Photo shooting menu > Photo flicker reduction
menu_path.z5ii: Photo shooting menu > Photo flicker reduction

one_liner: Times each shot to the peak of mains-frequency flicker (100/120 Hz).
what_it_does: Detects 100/120 Hz flicker from mains-powered lamps (fluorescent, mercury vapour, cheap LED drivers) and releases the shutter at the brightest point of the cycle, so exposure and colour stay consistent through a burst. It adds a small shutter lag and can slow or make bursts irregular. It does not fix high-frequency PWM LED banding - that's the next setting.

options.meaning: Flicker-timed release; green indicator next to FLICKER when detected.
options.use_when: Gyms, school halls, auditoriums with older lighting.
Daylight, theatrical lighting without mains flicker, any time you need zero lag.

when_to_change: If a test burst shows frames alternating brighter/darker or colour-shifting, turn it on.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light
suggested.value: ON if test bursts vary in brightness/colour; OFF if the rig is flicker-free
ON indoors under fluorescent/LED ceiling lights

body_differences: On all three. Z50II: in CH extended, frame rate takes priority (blackout only on first frame); in CH/CL, flicker reduction takes priority and frame rate may drop. Not active in HDR overlay, high-speed frame capture+, or Silent mode (Z50II).
gotchas: Doesn't work in Silent mode or HSFC+ (Z50II manual) - on the Z5II/Z50II that means mechanical/EFCS shutter.
Detection unreliable in bright scenes, dark backgrounds or decorative lighting; if results are poor, power-cycle while pointing at the light.
Long bursts in CH extended may not be fully corrected.
firmware_note: Z8 FW 2.10 fixed freezes/overexposure with auto bracketing when photo flicker reduction was on.
research_notes: Z8 burst-priority behaviour not read from the Z8 manual body.

menu_path.z8: Photo shooting menu > High-frequency flicker reduction
menu_path.z5ii: Photo shooting menu > High-frequency flicker reduction

one_liner: Fine-step shutter speeds to remove LED banding stripes (modes S and M).
what_it_does: Lets you adjust shutter speed in tiny steps (e.g. 1/512.0 s instead of 1/500 s) in S and M so you can match the PWM frequency of LED stage lights or screens and make banding disappear. You watch the magnified live view and nudge the speed until the stripes go away.

options.meaning: Shutter speed shown as denominator with one decimal; fine steps.
options.use_when: LED stage rigs, LED walls/screens, LED-lit halls with banding.
Everything else.

when_to_change: The moment you see horizontal stripes in live view under LED light.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light
suggested.value: On; start near your target (1/320-1/500 s per your Bharatanatyam speeds) and fine-tune until bands vanish in magnified view; recheck when the lighting cue changes
On only if indoor LEDs band

Turning it off rounds the speed to the nearest standard value.

name: Vibration reduction (Normal / Sport / Off)

menu_path.z8: Photo shooting menu > Vibration reduction (also i menu)

one_liner: Stabilisation style: maximum (Normal), action-friendly (Sport), or Off.
what_it_does: Normal gives the most correction for static subjects; Sport gives a steadier, less 'floaty' viewfinder for tracking erratic subjects and is recommended for panning. In Normal/Sport, panning motion is not corrected, only the perpendicular axis. On the Z8/Z5II this drives in-body 5-axis IBIS plus lens VR; on the Z50II only VR lenses are stabilised.

options.meaning: Strongest stabilisation; image may 'jiggle' before release.
options.use_when: Static subjects handheld, macro, slow-shutter handheld.

options.meaning: Steadier framing, less lag; recommended for panning.
options.use_when: Birds, dancers, kids - anything you track.
Solidly locked tripod, especially for long exposures.

when_to_change: Sport for tracking, Normal for static handheld, Off on a locked-down tripod.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light
suggested.value: Sport (Normal for held poses at 1/160 s or slower)
Off on a solid tripod; Normal if the head is loose or it's windy

body_differences: Z8: 5-axis IBIS + lens VR. Z5II: 5-axis IBIS (Nikon: about 7.5 stops centre with 24-120 f/4 S) plus Focus-point VR option. Z50II: no IBIS - menu works only with VR lenses (the DX 16-50/18-140/50-250/12-28 PZ VR, 180-600, 70-200, MC 105); electronic VR is video-only.
gotchas: F-mount lenses with a VR switch on the FTZ II: VR must be set on the lens.
On the Z50II, primes like the Sigma 30/56 and 40mm f/2 have no stabilisation at all.
In Normal the view may drift before release - switch to Sport if distracting.
research_notes: Tripod advice ('Off on a locked tripod, Normal if not secured') is common Nikon guidance from older Z manuals and is not re-verified in the current manuals (Z50II VR page doesn't cover tripods).

name: Link VR to focus point (Focus-point VR)

menu_path.z5ii: Photo shooting menu > Link VR to focus point

one_liner: Z5II centres IBIS correction on your focus point, not the frame centre.
what_it_does: Normal IBIS is optimised for the frame centre, so off-centre subjects get less effective correction (Nikon rates the Z5II about 7.5 stops at centre vs 6.0 at the periphery). Linking VR to the focus point optimises correction at the active focus point, helping off-centre subjects at slow shutter speeds.

options.meaning: Correction optimised at the focus point.
options.use_when: Off-centre subjects at slow handheld speeds: dancers placed on thirds, macro with the point near the edge.

one_liner: Body and lens VR working together for extra stops - automatic, no menu.
what_it_does: On supporting bodies, Synchro VR coordinates in-body and lens VR instead of splitting axes between them, for a higher rated stabilization (Z8: 6.0 stops with Synchro VR versus 5.5 body-only, per Nikon USA). There is no setting to toggle; it runs whenever a compatible lens with current firmware is attached and VR is on.
when_to_change: Nothing to change - just know whether your combination supports it.

suggested.value: Irrelevant on a locked tripod; VR off per your tripod practice.
Z 70-200 VR S (lens firmware 1.20+) on Z8: active. Z 180-600: support not verified.
Z MC 105 VR S support not verified; Nikon says VR effect shrinks at close range anyway.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light
suggested.value: Only relevant with the 70-200 VR S; F lenses on the FTZ II cannot use Synchro VR.

body_differences: Z8 and Z5 II are listed in Nikon's Synchro VR support article (as quoted publicly; the Nikon page itself is robots-blocked). Z50 II has no IBIS, so it cannot use Synchro VR. F lenses on the FTZ II never use Synchro VR (Nikon FTZ compatibility guide).
gotchas: Not a menu setting.
Lens firmware matters: the Z 70-200 f/2.8 VR S gained Synchro VR in lens firmware 1.20.
Support for the 180-600 and MC 105 is not verified; Nikon's list as quoted was truncated.
research_notes: Updated by main session from evidence gathered in the lens and body research: Nikon firmware notes for the 70-200 (1.20 added Synchro VR), a Jan 2026 forum quote of Nikon support article 000066751 listing Z8 and Z5 II, and Nikon USA's Z8 6.0-stop Synchro VR figure. The earlier claim that the 180-600 is not compatible came from the owner's notes, not a source, and is no longer asserted.

sources.name: Nikon Download Center: NIKKOR Z 70-200mm f/2.8 VR S firmware 1.22
sources.findings: Version 1.20 added Z 9 features including synchro VR ('Camera and lens VR are synchronized for improved vibration reduction'). 1.21 fixed focus-position display/recall beep issues; 1.22 improved focus tracking while zooming. Applies to lens firmware 1.10–1.21.

sources.name: FredMiranda forum thread 'Nikon IBIS + VR: Which lenses work & how?' (post #10, ekam, 2026-01-07) quoting Nikon support article 000066751
sources.findings: Quotes Nikon's Synchro VR support article (https://www.nikonimgsupport.com/eu/BV_article?articleNo=000066751&ctry=gb&lang=en_GB, which could not be fetched: robots-blocked). Compatible cameras: Z9, Z8, Z6III, Z5II, Zf, ZR. Synchro VR runs when a compatible lens is on a compatible body with body stabilization on. Visible lens entries: Z 28-400 VR, Z 70-200 f/2.8 VR S (marked with an unexplained asterisk), Z 100-400 VR S, Z 400 f/2.8 TC VR S; the quoted list is truncated ('...Show more'), so absence of a lens proves nothing.

name: Non-CPU lens data
one_liner: Tell the body a manual lens's focal length and aperture.
what_it_does: Stores focal length, maximum aperture and an optional name (up to 36 characters) per lens number for non-CPU lenses, so shooting data and EXIF show something useful. On IBIS bodies the entered focal length is widely understood to set the IBIS correction for manual lenses, so a wrong value weakens stabilisation.

options.use_when: One slot per lens: Thypoch 28, Zeiss 35 ZF.2 (if unchipped), Voigtlander 58 (if unchipped), etc.
Always set before shooting a manual lens on the Z8/Z5II.
Set to the lens's f-number.
Lets you filter shots by lens later.

when_to_change: Every time you mount a different unchipped lens - assign 'Non-CPU lens data' to a button or My Menu for quick switching.

suggested.value: Set correct lens number (VR off on tripod anyway)
Set lens number for the Laowa 65 or Tokina 100 if unchipped

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light
suggested.value: Set lens number if using the Thypoch 28

body_differences: Available on all three. On the Z50II (no IBIS) it only affects EXIF/shooting data.
gotchas: Only needed for lenses with no electronic contacts; chipped manual lenses (e.g. ZF.2/SL II-S CPU versions on the FTZ II) pass data automatically.
Forgetting to switch slots writes the wrong lens to EXIF and may mis-set IBIS.
research_notes: The IBIS-uses-entered-focal-length link is not stated on the Z50II page and was not read from the Z8/Z5II manuals - treat as likely, verify. Whether the Thypoch Simera 28 Z-mount has electronic contacts was not checked.

one_liner: Auto-steps focus from near to far for focus stacking.
what_it_does: Takes up to 300 frames while stepping focus from your starting point towards infinity, for stacking in software. You set number of shots, step width, interval, first-frame exposure lock, electronic shutter, and whether focus resets afterwards. Requires an AF lens (camera drives focus).

options.meaning: Max frames; stops early at infinity.
options.use_when: Overshoot - extras are cheap.

options.meaning: Focus move per frame; Nikon advises 5 or lower.
options.use_when: Smaller steps for macro (shallow DOF).
00 without flash; longer for flash recycle.
ON for changing light (landscapes).
Macro on tripod (Z5II/Z50II); Z8 always electronic.

options.value: Focus position auto reset / Starting storage folder
options.meaning: Return focus to start; new folder per sequence.
options.use_when: Repeat stacks; easy sorting.

when_to_change: Tripod macro or near-far landscapes needing more depth than f/8 gives.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light

suggested.value: Step 5, 10-20 shots, first-frame exposure lock ON, f/5.6-f/8
Not handheld - use on tripod: step 2-3, 30-100 shots, MC 105 at f/5.6-f/8

body_differences: All three. Z8 FW 3.00 can combine focus shift with pixel shift. Z8 has no mechanical shutter so e-shutter option is moot.
gotchas: Start focus slightly in front of the nearest point - sequence runs towards infinity.
Use apertures wider than f/8-f/11 (Nikon) to avoid diffraction softening.
Manual-focus lenses (Laowa 65, Tokina 100, AF-D 60 Micro on FTZ II) can't be driven - use a focusing rail instead.
Not combinable with HSFC+, bracketing, interval timer, multiple exposure, HDR, bulb.
firmware_note: Z8 FW 3.00: focus shift + pixel shift combination; fixed a rare focus-shift freeze.
research_notes: Z8/Z5II option lists assumed to match the Z50II (not read).

one_liner: Shoots stills automatically at set intervals; can also build a time-lapse.
what_it_does: Takes a set number of shots at a fixed interval from a start time. Options include exposure smoothing (gradual exposure changes), electronic shutter, interval priority, refocus before each shot, AE bracketing per interval and an in-camera time-lapse movie built from the stills.

options.use_when: Moonrise every 10-30 s; sunset sequences.

options.meaning: Matches exposure to previous frame (needs Auto ISO in M).
options.use_when: Day-to-night transitions.

options.meaning: Keeps the interval in P/A even if exposure gets long.
options.use_when: Time-lapse where rhythm matters.
OFF for moon/landscape (keep focus fixed).

options.meaning: Bracket each interval or make a movie too.
options.use_when: High-contrast scenes / quick shareable time-lapse.

when_to_change: Any timed sequence on a tripod.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light

suggested.value: Interval 3-5 s, exposure smoothing ON, focus before each shot OFF
Interval 10-20 s, 60-200 shots, manual exposure, focus before each shot OFF, VR off

body_differences: All three. Z50II e-shutter option overrides d6.
gotchas: Interval must exceed exposure + write time or intervals get skipped.
E-shutter still makes a sound unless volume is 0, even in Silent mode.
Moon moves its own diameter in about 2 minutes - at 280mm reframe or plan the path.
research_notes: Moon-motion tip is general astronomy, not from a fetched source.

name: Pixel shift shooting

menu_path.z8: Photo shooting menu > Pixel shift shooting
menu_path.z5ii: Photo shooting menu > Pixel shift shooting

one_liner: Shifts the sensor between frames for higher-resolution, low-moire composites.
what_it_does: Takes a series of RAW frames with the sensor moved by sub-pixel amounts, then merges them in Nikon NX Studio on a computer into a higher-resolution image (Nikon cites up to about 180 MP on the Z8). Needs a static subject and a rock-solid tripod. On the Z8, FW 3.00 can combine it with focus shift or AE bracketing.

options.meaning: How many shifted frames and timing.
options.use_when: More frames = more resolution and colour accuracy, more chance of movement artefacts.

options.value: Z8: combine with focus shift or AE bracketing (FW 3.00)
options.use_when: Static macro (MC 105) or high-contrast architecture.

options.value: Z8: WB lock at first shot, new folder per sequence, self-timer (FW 3.00)
options.use_when: Always - sorting and merging is easier.

when_to_change: Static, tripod-mounted subjects only: architecture, art reproduction, still-life macro.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light

suggested.value: Only for windless, cloud-free static scenes

body_differences: Z8: added FW 2.00; FW 3.00 adds focus-shift/AE-bracket combination. Z5II: listed in its Photo shooting menu. Z50II: not available.
gotchas: Merging happens in NX Studio, not in camera.
Any movement (leaves, water, people) causes artefacts.
Uses the IBIS mechanism - VR has no role here.

name: Sensor shield behavior at power off

menu_path.z8: Setup menu > Sensor shield behavior at power off

one_liner: Z8 closes a shield over the sensor when off, keeping dust out.
what_it_does: The Z8 has a thin shield in front of the sensor (it has no mechanical shutter). Set it to close at power-off so dust lands on the shield instead of the sensor during lens changes - but only if you switch off before changing lenses.

options.meaning: Shield closes when the camera is turned off.
options.use_when: Default choice for field use, especially changing lenses outdoors.
Wet sensor cleaning (or use Clean image sensor maintenance).

when_to_change: Set to close once; switch off before every lens change.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light

body_differences: Z8 only. Z5II and Z50II have mechanical shutters and no such setting.
gotchas: Never touch the shield - it is more fragile than a mechanical shutter; use only a hand blower.
If the power switch is on 'sleep'/standby or the card is still writing, the shield may stay open - turn fully OFF.
Doesn't help if you change lenses with the camera on.
research_notes: Exact option labels from Have Camera Will Travel, not from the Z8 manual body.

name: Clean image sensor
one_liner: Ultrasonic shake that knocks loose dust off the sensor.
what_it_does: Vibrates the sensor filter to remove loose dust, on demand or automatically at shutdown. It won't remove sticky spots - those need a blower or wet clean.

options.use_when: After a dusty outing or before a critical f/11+ landscape.

options.value: Clean at shutdown (Z5II default since FW 1.02) / off
options.use_when: Leave on.

when_to_change: Run Clean now when a test shot of sky at f/16 shows spots.

suggested.scenario: Stage dance in low LED light

suggested.value: Clean at shutdown (dust shows at small apertures)

body_differences: Z8 and Z5II only. The Z50II setup menu has no Clean image sensor item (Image Dust Off ref photo only).
gotchas: On the Z8, use this maintenance mode (or set the shield to stay open) before a wet clean.
firmware_note: Z5II FW 1.02 changed the default to 'Clean at shutdown'.
